Since my vision get less fatigued with dark windows, I'd like to establish a dark background in my gnuplot terminal. Establishing a dark square beneath the plot would be a solution, if only this would not influence readability (dark lines on dark background...).

I don't want to spend my day in discovering color combinations, however by flipping the terminal color I would acquire exactly what I need: dark background and readable plots.

Does anyone know a command for flipping the terminal, or the name of an interactive terminal (supported by GNU/Linux) which facilitates color flipping?

Thanks in advance.

Many terminals (including png and wxt) possess background option.

You can establish dark background, for instance:

set terminal wxt background '#00222222'

And then alter border/axis color to something light, for instance:

set style line 101 lc rgb '#808080' lt 1 lw 1  
set border 3 front ls 101

I don't know about automatic 'color flipping', but this seems like a pretty good workaround. You can find some fascinating information in Ease your plotting with config-snippets article.

See gnuplot-colorbrewer for some predefined color palettes.

I wish to discover the final term between slashes in a url. For instance, locate "nika" in "/gallery/haha/nika/7907/08-2015"

I composed this in my python script:

>>> text = '/gallery/haha/nika/7907/08-2015'  
>>> re.findall(r'/[a-zA-Z]*/$', text)  

but I received an empty list:

[]  

And if I eliminate that dollar sign:

>>> re.findall(r'/[a-zA-Z]*/', text)  

The output list is not empty but '/haha/' is omitted:

['/gallery/', '/nika/']  

Anyone aware why?  

Use lookarounds as in  

re.findall(r'(?<=/)[a-zA-Z]*(?=/)', text)  

See demo  

$ signifies end of string so you are obtaining empty string.  

haha is absent because you are capturing / and so / is not left for haha. When you employ lookarounds it is a 0 width assertion and it does not consume / and so all are captured.

I have announced a class Triangle in Python which accepts base and height as __init__ parameters and has a method area that calculates and returns the area of the triangle. The __eq__ method of the Triangle class evaluates the area of the triangles and return the value. The class is established as below:

class Shape(object):  
    def area(self):  
        raise AttributeException("Subclasses should override this method.")  

class Triangle(Shape):  
    def __init__(self, base, height):  
        """  
        base = base of the triangle.  
        height = height of the triangle  
        """  
        self.base = base  
        self.height = height  
    def area(self):  
        return (self.base * self.height)/2  
    def __str__(self):  
        return 'Triangle with base ' + str(self.base) + ' and height ' + str(self.height)  
    def __eq__(self, other):  
        """  
        Two triangles are equivalent if their area is equal  
        """  
        return (self.area() == other.area())  

Now I executed the program and created two instances to Triangle t1 and t3 , and gave them different base and height but their area is equivalent. So t1 == t3 should be True which is returned as True only. But strangely, t1 > t3 is also returned as True , which I don't comprehend why?  

>>> t1 = Triangle(3,4)  
>>> t3 = Triangle(2, 6)  
>>> t1.area()  
6  
>>> t3.area()  
6  
>>> t1 == t3  
True  
>>> t1 > t3  
True  
>>> t1 < t3  
False  
>>>  

Although I can't find a source on this, it appears as if Python 2 uses the id to compare two objects if you don't define the respective magic methods yourself.

>>> t1 = Triangle(3, 4)  
>>> t3 = Triangle(2, 6)  
>>> t1 > t3  
False  
>>> t1 < t3  
True  
>>> t1 = Triangle(3, 4)  
>>> t1 > t3  
True  
>>> t1 < t3  
False  

This behavior isn't ensured as id doesn't guarantee you to assign increasing numbers to objects created later, but it does generally seem to function in CPython 2.7, since id will provide you the physical address of the object.  

You will notice that before the redefinition of t1 , id(t1) < id(t3) , while afterwards, the opposite is the case.

Multisampling is a method of implementing full screen anti-aliasing (FSAA) in 3D applications. I need to utilize multisampling in my OpenGL program, which is currently integrated in a wxWidgets GUI. Is there a method to do this? Please reply only if you know the specific steps to accomplish this.

I'm aware of activating multisampling using WGL (Win32 extensions to OpenGL). However, since my OpenGL program isn't coded in MFC (and I desire the code to be multi-platform portable), that's not an alternative for me.

I eventually got Multisampling functioning with my wxWidgets OpenGL program. It's a bit chaotic right now, but here's how:

wxWidgets doesn't possess Multisampling support in their stable releases right now (latest version at this time is 2.8.8 ). But, it's accessible as a patch and also through their daily snapshot. (The latter is encouraging, since it indicates that the patch has been approved and should appear in future stable releases if there are no issues.)

So, there are 2 alternatives:

1. Download and compile from their daily snapshot .

2. Obtain the patch for your functioning wxWidgets installation.

I discovered the 2nd alternative to be less inconvenient, since I don't want to disrupt my functioning installation as much as possible. If you don't know how to patch on Windows, see this .

At the very least, for Windows, the patch will alter the following files:

$(WX_WIDGETS_ROOT)/include/wx/glcanvas.h  
$(WX_WIDGETS_ROOT)/include/wx/msw/glcanvas.h  
$(WX_WIDGETS_ROOT)/src/msw/glcanvas.cpp  

After patching, recompile the wxWidgets libraries.

To activate multisampling in your wxWidgets OpenGL program, slight modifications to the code are needed.

An attribute list needs to be passed to the wxGLCanvas constructor:

int attribList[] = {WX_GL_RGBA,  
                    WX_GL_DOUBLEBUFFER,  
                    WX_GL_SAMPLE_BUFFERS, GL_TRUE, // Multi-sampling  
                    WX_GL_DEPTH_SIZE, 16,  
                    0, 0};  

If you were already utilizing an attribute list, then add the line with GL_SAMPLE_BUFFERS, GL_TRUE to it. Otherwise, add this attribute list definition to your code.

Then alter your wxGLCanvas constructor to accept this attribute list as a parameter:

myGLFrame::myGLFrame    // Derived from wxGLCanvas  
(  
    wxWindow *parent,  
    wxWindowID id,  
    const wxPoint& pos,  
    const wxSize& size,  
    long style,  
    const wxString& name  
)  
: wxGLCanvas(parent, (wxGLCanvas*) NULL, id, pos, size, style, name, attribList)  
{  
    // ...  
}  

After the wxGLCanvas element is generated, multisampling is activated by default. To disable or enable it at will, use the related OpenGL functions:

glEnable(GL_MULTISAMPLE);  
glDisable(GL_MULTISAMPLE);  

Multisampling should now function with the wxWidgets OpenGL program. Hopefully, it should be backed in the stable release of wxWidgets soon, making this information irrelevant :-)

com.microsoft.azure.CloudException: Status code 403, {"error":{"code":"AuthorizationFailed","message":"The client '5c79ee27-#########-######91f8e3' with object id '5c79ee27-###########-#####91f8e3' does not possess authorization to execute action 'Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/listKeys/action' over scope '/subscriptions/758ad253-#######f07/resourceGroups/spcwestus/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/grsstorag'."}}: The client '5c79ee27-###########-#####91f8e3' with object id '5c79ee27-###########-#####91f8e3' does not possess authorization to execute action 'Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/listKeys/action' over scope '/subscriptions/758ad253-#######f07/resourceGroups/spcwestus/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/grsstorag'.

For most of the Storage Accounts I succeed in acquiring the keys. But for some of them the same error recurs. What does this signify?


From the error you faced, the server answered to your requests with HTTP 403 status code indicates that your request is Prohibited by the server.

HTTP 403 Status Code A server that receives valid credentials that are not sufficient to  
  gain access should reply with the 403 (Prohibited) status code (Section 6.5.3 of [RFC7231]).

This is most likely caused by some Role-Based Access Control measures that are in effect to stop your account from performing the list storage account key operations for specific storage accounts based on your allocated role.

You can utilize the Azure PowerShell cmdlet below to check whether the role designated to your particular object under the specified scope has the authority to list the storage account keys.

Get-AzureRmRoleAssignment -Scope "/subscriptions/758ad253-#######f07/resourceGroups/spcwestus/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/grsstorag" -ObjectId 5c79ee27-###########-#####91f8e3

Further information please consult the link below:

Use Role-Based Access Control to manage access to your Azure subscription resources

We possess a VB.NET project which I am performing some refactoring in. A lot of existing functions necessitate a userId to be passed in as a parameter. For example:

Private Function Foo(userId As Integer) As String  
    Return "Foo"  
End Function  

But presently, I have made this userId parameter no longer required in much of our code.  

I was contemplating I would just eliminate all the userId parameters from all of the functions that don't require them anymore, and attempt re-building the project to see what calling code needs to modify. To my astonishment though, the code built successfully.  

I discovered that you can call a function which returns a string and doesn't accept any parameters, but still pass in an Integer value. VB.NET builds/executes this code as if you were trying to invoke the function and then obtain the character from the String at the specified index. For example:  

Imports System  

Public Module MyModule  
    Private Function Foo() As String  
        Return "Foo"  
    End Function  

    Public Sub Main()  
        Console.WriteLine(Foo(0)) ' prints 'F'  
        Console.WriteLine(Foo(1)) ' prints 'o'  
    End Sub  
End Module  

( .NET Fiddle )  

I desire my build to fail in this situation. I have attempted using Option Strict On and Option Explicit On but neither seem to alter this behavior.  

Is there anyhow to make this kind of function invocation invalid in my VB.NET project?  

Create an overload with no parameters which is a copy of the original function in every other aspect.  

Public Function Foo() As String  
    Return "Foo"  
End Function  

Now modify the type of userId to something else (not Object or anything numeric etc.)  

Public Function Foo(userId As DateTime) As String  
    Return "Foo"  
End Function  

Since there is an overload with a parameter, the compiler believes you mean to call that, instead of indexing the chararray. So you have compile errors. Rectify the errors  

Then remove the original function.

perturbations.a:
We need to refresh our forms to be accessibility compliant. I am seeking for information on how to compose an inline error for a form select. I have the form field designated and have an inline error, but the readers do not announce the error.

Here is what we are utilizing

Security Question  
Select a Question  
What is your mother's maiden name?  
What's your town of birth?  
What is your father's middle name?  
What street did you reside on when you were 10 years old?  
r  
Please choose a security hint question.

So if the user doesn't select an option and submits we dynamically inject an error just after the form field as depicted above. This operates fine for inputs and text boxes, but for the select, the reader skips it.

I been studying different blogs and specs and have examined many times, don't use selects, but use radios or text boxes instead.

So any suggestions?

Your issue might be connected to the following bug: JAWS does not announce aria-describedby on select box in IE

This is also outlined on WebAim mailing list.

This is a bug, you have multiple options to avoid this bug:

* including the error text in the label

* ARIA21: Using Aria-Invalid to Indicate An Error Field

* SCR18: Providing client-side validation and alert

* Re-presenting a form with a summary of errors

* Providing error notification as the user enters data

* Including error notification information in the page title

For example, you can use aria-labelledby to target both the label and the error text.

Possessing the subsequent type:  
  
type MyType =  
    | MyType of string  
  
I attempted to execute this:  
  
let myFunc x =  
    let MyType y = x  
    y // Compilation error  
  
This results in a compilation error:  
  
The value or constructor y is not defined.  
  
Nonetheless, if I insert parentheses around MyType y, the code compiles.  
  
let myFunc x =  
    let (MyType y) = x  
    y // Compiles successfully  
  
What is the distinction between the two versions?  
  
The initial version declares a function named MyType with one parameter named y. This parameter is only available in the body of this function, so you receive an error when you attempt to access this parameter outside of the function.  
  
The subsequent version destructures a value with constructor named MyType, binding its content to identifier y. This identifier is then accessible until the current scope concludes.  
  
The parentheses as necessary to differentiate destructuring from function declaration.  
  
In this specific situation, you can simplify the destructuring by relocating it into the parameter list:  
  
let myFunc (MyType y) =  
    y

I possess a class which extends JFrame and forms the GUI of my application. I wish to use the GUI for two primary purposes:  

1. I want the user to be capable of providing values to the application.  

2. I want the GUI to exhibit values generated by my application.  

Considering my class has a multitude of GUI elements, the source file is already quite extensive and It does not appear like sound practice to bundle all the application code in with the GUI code. I'm contemplating what is the optimal way to structure my code? I believe there is a concern where requirement 1 creates a dependency from the GUI to the application code, and the second requirement does the inverse.  

So, I desire one class for my GUI which encompasses all my GUI related tasks. I then wish for another class for my application logic. I should then be able to invoke methods from the application logic class from the GUI and vice versa.  

Sounds like you are seeking a textbook MVC (Model-View-Controller) design pattern. I suggest you search "MVC Design Pattern" for summaries and use cases. That being said, you might want to place your application logic into a "Singleton" class (again, search "Singleton Design Pattern"). A properly implemented Singleton should be reachable from any other class in your code.  

Consider also a third intermediary class which operates solely for data storage, you place values into it for storage, and you retrieve values from it for work. This now forms 3 clear segments for your code, the Data (the Model), the GUI (the View), and the logic (the Controller). Voila, you've just established the MVC (Model-View-Controller) design pattern...

1. I want the user to have the ability to enter values to the program.  

2. I want the GUI to represent values formulated by my program.  

Considering my class has a multitude of GUI components, the source file is already relatively voluminous and It does not seem to be sound practice to enclose all the program code in with the GUI code. I'm reflecting on what is the finest way to structure my code? I believe there is a dilemma where requirement 1 establishes a dependency from the GUI to the program code, and the subsequent requirement does the opposite.  

So, I want one class for my GUI which holds all my GUI correlated tasks. I then intend for another class for my program logic. I should then be capable of calling methods from the program logic class from the GUI and vice versa.  

Sounds like you are searching for a textbook MVC (Model-View-Controller) design pattern. I suggest you query "MVC Design Pattern" for summaries and use cases. That being said, you might wish to position your program logic into a "Singleton" class (again, query "Singleton Design Pattern"). A properly fashioned Singleton should be reachable from any other class in your code.  

Consider also a third intermediate class which acts solely for data storage, you transfer values into it for storage, and you extract values from it for work. This now establishes 3 clear factions for your code, the Data (the Model), the GUI (the View), and the logic (the Controller). Voila, you've just created the MVC (Model-View-Controller) design pattern...

My comprehension is that it ascends the Object hierarchy searching for a declared method corresponding to the symbol, then descends looking for the lowest declared method_missing. This is much slower than a typical method call.

Is it feasible to intercept sent messages before this moment? I attempted overriding send, and this operates when the call to send is explicit, but not when it is implicit.

Not that I am aware of.

The most efficient bet is generally to use method_missing to dynamically add the method being called to the class so that the overhead is only ever incurred once. From that point forward it invokes the method like any other method.

Such as:

  def method_missing(name, str)

    # log something out when we invoke method_missing so we know it only occurs once
    puts "Defining method named: #{name}"

    # Define the new instance method
    self.class.class_eval <<-CODE
      def #{name}(arg1)
        puts 'you passed in: ' + arg1.to_s
      end
    CODE

    # Execute the instance method we just created to return the value on this first execution
    send name, str
  end
end

f = Foo.new
f.echo_string 'wtf'
f.echo_string 'hello'
f.echo_string 'yay!'

You can achieve this by creating distinct storyboards for each device and setting the entry point for the devices to the appropriate storyboard in your target summary.

Detailed directions follow.

Once you have developed an empty, universal application, you'll desire to create distinct storyboards for each device.

File -> New -> File -> User Interface -> Storyboard -> (MainStoryboard_iPad & MainStoryboard_iPhone)

Within each storyboard you'll have to insert at least one view controller. You can confirm functionality by dragging in a single view controller and a label for each storyboard (label one "iPad" and one "iPhone").

With the storyboards in position you need to add the code for the view controllers. Apple advises adding a distinct view controller for each device, but you might possibly share a single view controller if you truly wished to.

File -> New -> File -> ViewController -> (HomeViewController_iPad & HomeViewController_iPhone)

Navigate back to the respective storyboards, select the view controller you inserted, and set the view controllers (HomeViewController_iPad & HomeViewController_iPhone) in the identity inspector. Then add the referencing outlet by right clicking the view and dragging add referencing outlet onto the view controller and selecting view.

Finally, you need to set the entry point for each device. Navigate to your target summary and select the Main Storyboard for each device to the storyboards you have just developed.

At this moment, running the app will exhibit "iPad" and "iPhone" on the respective devices.
